verses.zh: 「众祭司啊，这诫命是传给你们的。
verses.en: “Now, you priests, this commandment is for you.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华说：你们若不听从，也不放在心上，将荣耀归与我的名，我就使咒诅临到你们，使你们的福分变为咒诅；因你们不把诫命放在心上，我已经咒诅你们了。
verses.en: If you do not listen and take seriously[NOTE:1] the need to honor my name,” says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, “I will send judgment[NOTE:2] on you and turn your blessings into curses—indeed, I have already done so because you are not taking it to heart.
notes: Heb “and if you do not place upon [the] heart”; KJV, NAB, NRSV “lay it to heart.”
Heb “the curse” (so NASB, NRSV); NLT “a terrible curse.”

verses.zh: 我必斥责你们的种子，又把你们牺牲的粪抹你们的脸上；你们要与粪一同除掉。
verses.en: I am about to discipline your children[NOTE:1] and will spread offal[NOTE:2] on your faces,[NOTE:3] the very offal produced at your festivals, and you will be carried away along with it.
notes: The phrase “discipline your children” is disputed. The LXX and Vulgate suppose זְרוֹעַ (zeroaʿ, “arm”) for the MT זֶרַע (zeraʿ, “seed”; hence, “children”). Then, for the MT גֹעֵר (goʿer, “rebuking”) the same versions suggest גָּרַע (garaʿ, “take away”). The resulting translation is “I am about to take away your arm” (cf. NAB “deprive you of the shoulder”). However, this reading is unlikely. It is common for a curse (v. 2) to fall on offspring (see, e.g., Deut 28:18, 32, 41, 53, 55, 57), but a curse never takes the form of a broken or amputated arm. It is preferable to retain the reading of the MT here.

The Hebrew term פֶרֶשׁ (feresh, “offal”) refers to the entrails as ripped out in preparing a sacrificial victim (BDB 831 s.v. פֶּרֶשׁ). This graphic term has been variously translated: “dung” (KJV, RSV, NRSV, NLT, NIV11); “refuse” (NKJV, NASB); “offal” (NEB, NIV84).
See Zech 3:3-4 for similar coarse imagery which reflects cultic disqualification.

verses.zh: 你们就知道我传这诫命给你们，使我与利未（或译：利未人）所立的约可以常存。这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: Then you will know that I sent this commandment to you so that my covenant[NOTE:1] may continue to be with Levi,” says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: My covenant refers to the priestly covenant through Aaron and his grandson Phinehas (see Exod 6:16-20; Num 25:10-13; Jer 33:21-22). The point here is to contrast the priestly ideal with the disgraceful manner in which it was being carried out in postexilic times.

verses.zh: 我曾与他立生命和平安的约。我将这两样赐给他，使他存敬畏的心，他就敬畏我，惧怕我的名。
verses.en: “My covenant with him was designed to bring life and peace. I gave its statutes to him to fill him with awe, and he indeed revered me and stood in awe before me.

verses.zh: 真实的律法在他口中，他嘴里没有不义的话。他以平安和正直与我同行，使多人回头离开罪孽。
verses.en: He taught what was true;[NOTE:1] sinful words were not found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and integrity, and he turned many people away from sin.
notes: Heb “True teaching was in his mouth”; cf. NASB, NRSV “True instruction (doctrine NAB) was in his mouth.”

verses.zh: 祭司的嘴里当存知识，人也当由他口中寻求律法，因为他是万军之耶和华的使者。
verses.en: For the lips of a priest should preserve knowledge of sacred things, and people should seek instruction from him[NOTE:1] because he is the messenger of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: Heb “from his mouth” (so NAB, NASB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 你们却偏离正道，使许多人在律法上跌倒。你们废弃我与利未所立的约。这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: You, however, have turned from the way. You have caused many to violate the law;[NOTE:1] you have corrupted the covenant with Levi,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: The definite article embedded within בַּתּוֹרָה (battorah) may suggest that the Torah is in mind and not just “ordinary” priestly instruction, though it might refer to the instruction previously mentioned (v. 7).
Or “the Levitical covenant.”

verses.zh: 所以我使你们被众人藐视，看为下贱；因你们不守我的道，竟在律法上瞻徇情面。」
verses.en: “Therefore, I have caused you to be ignored and belittled before all people to the extent that you are not following after me and are showing partiality in your[NOTE:1] instruction.”
notes: Heb “in the instruction” (so NASB). The Hebrew article is used here as a possessive pronoun (cf. NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 我们岂不都是一位父吗？岂不是一位　神所造的吗？我们各人怎么以诡诈待弟兄，背弃了　神与我们列祖所立的约呢？
verses.en: Do we not all have one father?[NOTE:1] Did not one God create us? Why do we betray one another, thus making light of the covenant of our ancestors?
notes: The rhetorical question Do we not all have one father? by no means teaches the “universal fatherhood of God,” that is, that all people equally are children of God. The reference to the covenant in v. 10 as well as to Israel and Judah (v. 11) makes it clear that the referent of “we” is God’s elect people.

verses.zh: 犹大人行事诡诈，并且在以色列和耶路撒冷中行一件可憎的事；因为犹大人亵渎耶和华所喜爱的圣洁（或译：圣地），娶事奉外邦神的女子为妻。
verses.en: Judah has become disloyal, and unspeakable sins have been committed in Israel and Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] For Judah has profaned[NOTE:2] the holy things that the Lord loves and has turned to a foreign god![NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Or perhaps “secularized”; cf. NIV “desecrated”; TEV, NLT “defiled”; CEV “disgraced.”

Heb “has married the daughter of a foreign god.” Marriage is used here as a metaphor to describe Judah’s idolatry, that is, her unfaithfulness to the Lord and “remarriage” to pagan gods. But spiritual intermarriage found expression in literal, physical marriage as well, as vv. 14-16 indicate.

verses.zh: 凡行这事的，无论何人（何人：原文是叫醒的，答应的），就是献供物给万军之耶和华，耶和华也必从雅各的帐棚中剪除他。
verses.en: May the Lord cut off from the community[NOTE:1] of Jacob every last person who does this,[NOTE:2] as well as the person who presents improper offerings to the Lord of Heaven’s Armies!
notes: Heb “tents,” used figuratively for the community here (cf. NCV, TEV); NLT “the nation of Israel.”

Heb “every man who does this, him who is awake and him who answers.” The idea seems to be a merism expressing totality, that is, everybody from the awakener to the awakened, thus “every last person who does this” (NLT similar); NIV “whoever he may be.”tc Heb “every man who does this, him who is awake and him who answers.” For “answers” the LXX suggests an underlying Hebrew text of עָנָה (ʿanah, “to be humbled”), and then the whole phrase is modified slightly: “until he is humbled.” This requires also that the MT עֵר (ʿer, “awake”) be read as עֵד (ʿed, “until”; here the LXX reads ἕως, heōs). The reading of the LXX is most likely an alteration to correct what is arguably a difficult text.

verses.zh: 你们又行了一件这样的事，使前妻叹息哭泣的眼泪遮盖耶和华的坛，以致耶和华不再看顾那供物，也不乐意从你们手中收纳。
verses.en: You also do this: You cover the altar of the Lord with tears[NOTE:1] as you weep and groan, because he no longer pays any attention to the offering nor accepts it favorably from you.
notes: You cover the altar of the Lord with tears. These tears are the false tears of hypocrisy, not genuine tears of repentance. The people weep because the Lord will not hear them, not because of their sin.

verses.zh: 你们还说：「这是为甚么呢？」因耶和华在你和你幼年所娶的妻中间作见证。她虽是你的配偶，又是你盟约的妻，你却以诡诈待她。
verses.en: Yet you ask, “Why?” The Lord is testifying against you on behalf of the wife you married when you were young,[NOTE:1] to whom you have become unfaithful even though she is your companion and wife by law.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the Lord is a witness between you and [between] the wife of your youth.”

Though there is no explicit reference to marriage vows in the OT (but see Job 7:13; Prov 2:17; Ezek 16:8), the term law (Heb “covenant”) here asserts that such vows or agreements must have existed. References to divorce documents (e.g., Deut 24:1-3; Jer 3:8) also presuppose the existence of marriage documents.

verses.zh: 虽然　神有灵的余力能造多人，他不是单造一人吗？为何只造一人呢？乃是他愿人得虔诚的后裔。所以当谨守你们的心，谁也不可以诡诈待幼年所娶的妻。
verses.en: No one who has even a small portion of the Spirit in him does this.[NOTE:1] What did our ancestor[NOTE:2] do when seeking a child from God? Be attentive, then, to your own spirit, for one should not be disloyal to the wife he took in his youth.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and not one has done, and a remnant of the spirit to him.” The very elliptical nature of the statement suggests it is proverbial. The present translation represents an attempt to clarify the meaning of the statement (cf. NASB).

Heb “the one.” This is an oblique reference to Abraham who sought to obtain God’s blessing by circumventing God’s own plan for him by taking Hagar as wife (Gen 16:1-6). The result of this kind of intermarriage was, of course, disastrous (Gen 16:11-12).
The wife he took in his youth probably refers to the first wife one married (cf. NCV “the wife you married when you were young”).

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神说：「休妻的事和以强暴待妻的人都是我所恨恶的！所以当谨守你们的心，不可行诡诈。」这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: “I hate divorce,”[NOTE:1] says the Lord God of Israel, “and the one who is guilty of violence,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies. “Pay attention to your conscience, and do not be unfaithful.”
notes: Though the statement “I hate divorce” may (and should) be understood as a comprehensive biblical principle, the immediate context suggests that the divorce in view is that of one Jewish person by another in order to undertake subsequent marriages. The injunction here by no means contradicts Ezra’s commands to Jewish men to divorce their heathen wives (Ezra 9-10).tc The verb שָׂנֵא (saneʾ) appears to be a third person form, “he hates,” which makes little sense in the context, unless one emends the following word to a third person verb as well. Then one might translate, “he [who] hates [his wife] [and] divorces her…is guilty of violence.” A similar translation is advocated by M. A. Shields, “Syncretism and Divorce in Malachi 2, 10-16, ” ZAW 111 (1999): 81-85. However, it is possible that the first person pronoun אָנֹכִי (ʾanokhi, “I”) has accidentally dropped from the text after כִּי (ki). If one restores the pronoun, the form שָׂנֵא can be taken as a participle and the text translated, “for I hate” (so NAB, NASB, NRSV, NLT).

Heb “him who covers his garment with violence” (similar ASV, NRSV). Here “garment” is a metaphor for appearance and “violence” a metonymy of effect for cause. God views divorce as an act of violence against the victim.

verses.zh: 你们用言语烦琐耶和华，你们还说：「我们在何事上烦琐他呢？」因为你们说：「凡行恶的，耶和华眼看为善，并且他喜悦他们」；或说：「公义的　神在哪里呢？」
verses.en: You have wearied the Lord with your words. But you say, “How have we wearied him?” Because you say, “Everyone who does evil is good in the Lord’s opinion,[NOTE:1] and he delights in them,” or, “Where is the God of justice?”
notes: Heb “in the eyes of the Lord.”
